Summary: Manipulation is influence that bypasses honesty and consent, steering people toward a choice they would not freely make. Scripture contrasts it with persuasion that tells the truth and respects the other person's freedom: Paul insists he did not use flattery or hidden motives, and Jesus never coerced belief. Christians are called to spot manipulation - in leaders, in marketing, in relationships, even in their own hearts - and to replace it with plain speech, fair dealing, and respect for conscience.
